candidates.title: A 210 Megaparsec Ionized Structure at z = 6.8 Revealed by an Astrophysics Foundation Model
candidates.abstract: Abstract Reionization is the last major transition in the Universe that transforms the intergalactic medium (IGM) from neutral to highly ionized, yet its spatial structure remains poorly constrained. Using an astrophysics foundation model trained for James Webb Space Telescope datasets, we identify a luminous galaxy at redshift $z=7.567$ showing significant Ly$\alpha$ transmission at $z=6.80\pm0.07$. This transmission, named ``the First Ly$\alpha$ transmission in the Reionization Epoch at $z\sim7$" (FL$\alpha$RE-z7), indicates a cosmological-scale ionized structure extending over $210.5^{+55.7}_{-53.5}$ comoving Megaparsecs at cosmic dawn. The hydrogen neutral fraction of the ionized structure is $x_{\rm HI}=(2.07^{+0.29}_{-0.30})\times10^{-6}$, about $10^5$ times lower than the cosmic mean at similar redshifts $(x_{\rm HI}\approx0.4)$. Cosmological simulations suggest a probability of $\approx10^{-5}$ for a random sightline to reproduce the transmission. We find no significant galaxy overdensity associated with the transmission region, in tension with canonical inside-out reionization models. FL$\alpha$RE-z7 severely challenges existing reionization models in the standard $\Lambda$CDM Universe, indicating extreme spatial fluctuation in ionizing radiation or IGM temperature. Our result marks the first example of a foundation model discovering a previously unpredicted astrophysical phenomenon, demonstrating the power of deep learning methods for mining large astronomical datasets and finding unexpected new astrophysics.

candidates.title: BEYOND LEGAL REASONING: RECONSTRUCTING ETHICAL REASONING IN THE EXAMINATION AND ADJUDICATION OF CASES INVOLVING VIOLATIONS OF THE CODE OF ETHICS FOR ELECTION ORGANIZERS
candidates.abstract: Election integrity depends not only on compliance with legal rules but also on the ethical quality of election administrators’ conduct. Against this background, this article examines the relationship between legal reasoning and ethical reasoning in the examination and adjudication of alleged violations of the Code of Ethics for Election Administrators by the Election Organizer Honorary Council (DKPP). Using normative legal research with statutory, conceptual, and case approaches, the article analyzes DKPP decisions through Neil MacCormick’s theory of legal reasoning, Matthew Silverstein’s account of ethical reasoning, and John Rawls’s reflective equilibrium. The analysis shows that DKPP reasoning does not operate as a simple application of rules to facts. It involves the construction of relevant facts, identification and interpretation of legal norms, use of ethical principles, normative evaluation, and justification of sanctions. The article proposes an ethical-legal reasoning model that integrates legal boundaries, substantive ethical evaluation, and proportionality testing. The model is intended to strengthen the coherence, consistency, transparency, and accountability of DKPP decisions.

candidates.title: An implementation case study for Cascaded Case-Management Training and surge staffing intervention during Malawi’s 2022-2023 Outbreak
candidates.abstract: Abstract Background : Between 2022 and 2024 Malawi experienced the largest and deadliest cholera outbreak in its history, with more than 59,000 cases and an overall case fatality rate (CFR) of 3%. The outbreak was compounded by successive tropical cyclones and coincided with active COVID-19 and polio responses, exposing a two-decade capacity gap in cholera case management. In December 2022 the outbreak was declared a national public health emergency. Methods: We conducted an implementation case study of a three-component intervention delivered in February 2023: rapid cascaded case-management training, deployment of repurposed clinical surge staff, and facility-based mentorship at cholera treatment centres/units (CTCs/CTUs). Ten master trainers, trained a 46-member training-of-trainers (ToT), who then cascaded training to 600 clinicians across five parallel sites (Mzuzu, Lilongwe, Mponela, Blantyre and Liwonde) over 17 days. Knowledge was assessed with paired pre- and post-training tests (25 items). Linear mixed-effects models evaluated changes in test scores by cadre, time and training site. Multivariable logistic regression, adjusted for age, sex and district, estimated adjusted odds ratios (AORs) for mortality across pre-intervention (January 2022 – January 2023), active-intervention (February 2023) and post-intervention (March – December 2023) phases, using the national cholera line list. Results: We trained and deployed 572 healthcare workers. Paired knowledge data were available for 475 cascaded-training participants (17% attrition). Mean knowledge gain was 24.8% for the ToT cohort and 20.0% for the cascaded cohort; test-score improvements were highly significant overall (p<0.001) and uniform across cadres and sites (time × cadre interaction p=0.405 for ToT; p=0.990 for cascaded training). Compared with the pre-intervention phase, the odds of mortality among recorded cholera cases fell by 36% during the active-intervention phase (AOR 0.64; 95% CI 0.53–0.77; p<0.001) and by 14% in the post-intervention phase (AOR 0.86; 95% CI 0.73–1.01; p=0.067). Increasing age (AOR 1.03 per year; 95% CI 1.03–1.04; p<0.001) and male sex (AOR 1.45; 95% CI 1.28–1.63; p<0.001) were independent predictors of mortality. Conclusion : A cascaded case-management training package coupled with clinical surge staffing and facility-based mentorship is a feasible, scalable and plausibly effective response option for acute cholera outbreaks in resource-limited health systems.

candidates.title: A Layout-Aware Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Mitigating Hallucination in Turkish Texts: Evidence from the Turkish Official Gazette
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) hallucinate, which limits their use in domains with little tolerance for error, such as law. We present a layout-aware hybrid retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system for answering questions over 30 issues of the Turkish Official Gazette published in July 2025. The pipeline uses IBM Docling for hierarchical layout analysis and indexes content in PostgreSQL/pgvector with a local multilingual embedding model combined with a lexical index; response synthesis is delegated to claude-sonnet-5 under a citation-constrained prompt. On 33 questions written by the first author, the system answered 17 and declined 16 (coverage 51.5%). Among the answered questions, the hallucination rate was 4.2%, and citation accuracy was 81.8% (n = 11); Hit-Rate@8 was 0.786 on the 14 questions with labeled evidence. A zero-shot baseline gave a verifiable answer to one of 33 questions. In a retrieval ablation, replacing flat PDF text extraction with Docling raised Hit-Rate@8 from 0.21 to 0.79, whereas structural chunking and hybrid retrieval showed no consistent additional gain. A single legal expert rated 30 of 33 responses fully correct. Because the evaluation set is small, covers one month, and was rated by one expert, the results are exploratory and apply to this corpus.

candidates.title: In-silico Tandem Mass Spectral Libraries for the Blood Exposome and Metabolomics Workbench Databases: Application of Gemini Large Language Model
candidates.abstract: Human body contains endogenous metabolites, nutrients and xenobiotics chemicals. These chemicals can be detected in a biospecimen using high-resolution mass spectrometry instruments, yielding metabolomic and exposomic datasets. Mass spectral libraries are critical components of these workflows to annotate experimental data with chemical information. In this data descriptor, we report mass spectral libraries for human-relevant small molecules, that are generated using Google Gemini large-language model. Using an optimized chain-of-thought prompt and instructions, we have generated mass spectra for each compound at high/medium/low energy fragmentation level. Each spectrum was reported in the NIST MSP text format for easy to use by metabolomics software. These libraries cover 91,231 unique 2D structures from the Blood Exposome Database and the Metabolomics Workbench data repository. Technical validation was shown by comparing the Gemini-generated spectra against NIST 23 mass spectral database, which demonstrated 55% accuracy. LLMs represent a useful and accessible tool for expanding in-silico spectral libraries to annotate compounds in the HRMS data for human biospecimens and may accelerate the compound annotation in metabolomics and exposomics.

candidates.title: GraphRAG Retrieval of Regulatory Knowledge: An Empirical Evaluation for Ecuadorian Tax Legislation Query Answering
candidates.abstract: Tax regulation in Ecuador changes constantly, and the resulting information is scattered across laws, regulations, resolutions, forms, and annexes with strong ties across meaning and time. We compare four retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) strategies for question answering over Ecuadorian tax legislation (vector-only, GraphRAG, hybrid, and agentic retrieval) in a system that supports text, speech, and image inputs and combines a tax knowledge graph, dense vector search, and three agents that refine, validate, and plan each query’s strategy. Following a Design Science Research approach informed by a SALSA literature review, the system was tested on a curated 51-document corpus using 100 text-only tax queries across the four retrieval modes and two cloud generator models (gemma4:31b-cloud and gpt-oss:20b-cloud), for 800 RAGAS-judged executions, plus a Likert-scale review by five domain specialists. Speech- and image-input performance was not evaluated in this benchmark. Graph-only retrieval was weakest on all five RAGAS metrics (Context Precision = 0.02), while hybrid gave the best balance (Faithfulness = 0.67, Answer Relevancy = 0.64, Context Precision = 0.52, Context Recall = 0.76) at the lowest latency (2.66 s). Faithfulness depended more on the generator model than on retrieval mode (0.78 vs. 0.47). No strategy won on every metric, so architecture choice in dynamic regulatory domains should follow operational priority rather than a single universally optimal setup.

candidates.title: Cross-Island Transferability of Multi-Horizon Probabilistic Coastal Sargassum Occurrence Forecasts: A Frozen-Model Evaluation from Puerto Rico to the Dominican Republic
candidates.abstract: Satellite observations reveal the offshore distribution of pelagic Sargassum, but predicting its occurrence at individual Caribbean coastlines remains challenging where local observational records are limited. This study tests whether forecasts developed on one Caribbean island can transfer to another without retraining or recalibration. Satellite-derived predictors from the 0–10, 10–50, and 50–100 km offshore bands were evaluated at one-, two-, and four-week horizons. Rolling-origin validation in Puerto Rico selected Random Forest models at one and two weeks and a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN1D) ensemble with Platt calibration at four weeks. Frozen pipelines were applied unchanged at nine Dominican Republic sites and evaluated against 283 station-week targets. Puerto Rico 2026 provided independent testing. At one and two weeks, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC AUC) values were 0.745 and 0.757, area under the precision-recall curve (PR AUC) values were 0.689 and 0.687, and Brier Skill Score (BSS) values were +0.110 and +0.059. After transfer, ROC AUC values were 0.686 and 0.663, PR AUC values were 0.548 and 0.509, and BSS values were +0.098 and +0.056. Site removal did not eliminate short-horizon skill, and BSS remained positive by year. Transfer was clearest at one and two weeks, suggesting potential value for targeted coastal Sargassum monitoring, field verification, and response planning.

candidates.title: Regulating LLM training under EU copyright law and its linguistic implications for smaller languages such as Estonian
candidates.abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and text and data mining (TDM) technologies has become a crucial factor in supporting linguistic diversity of smaller languages, such as Estonian. However, the growing reliance on large-scale data processing raises significant legal and ethical challenges, particularly concerning the lawful use of copyrighted materials to train AI systems. While the European Union has introduced regulatory instruments such as the AI Act and the Copyright Directive to address these concerns, the intersection of AI development, TDM, and intellectual property rights remains insufficiently resolved. This research aims to explore how AI-driven text and data mining can both comply with European copyright law and actively contribute to the preservation and wider use of the Estonian language. The authors investigate this research topic from the perspective of the Estonian language, enmeshed within Estonian cultural norms and parameters. The analysis examines the legal and economic appropriateness of enabling the training of generative AI-based large language models (LLMs) in the Estonian language as a means of promoting the language and assuring its appropriate use in digital environments, thereby contributing to its long-term relevance. Methodologically, the study combines a comparative analysis of EU, US, and Asian legal frameworks with a theoretical evaluation of existing models for balancing innovation and rights protection. The article seeks to provide concrete recommendations for developing AI and data mining practices that enhance linguistic innovation while safeguarding creators’ rights, thereby contributing to Estonia’s digital and cultural resilience within the EU’s evolving AI ecosystem.

candidates.title: How Heterogeneous Is Homo Silicus? Measuring Risk-Preference Dispersion in Populations of Large Language Model Agents
candidates.abstract: Large language models are increasingly deployed as autonomous economic agents, and prior work observes that agent populations display less behavioural variation than human populations. This study measures that observation directly for the risk domain. It asks how much durable dispersion in elicited risk preference exists between agents built on a single model, whether persona conditioning creates more, and how that dispersion compares with human test–retest benchmarks. Variation is decomposed into within-agent noise across repeated queries and between-agent dispersion within a model; the difference between the two model families is reported as a fixed contrast. Agent identity is manipulated between two conditions: no conditioning beyond the sampling process (S0), and a synthetic persona describing background only (S3). All claims are scoped to the two models named below, at the decoding settings stated, on the canonical Holt–Laury payoff scale, at the access dates recorded. No claim is made about language models in general.

candidates.title: Democratizing reliable knowledge-seeking with MyGPT: a privacy-first, open-source retrieval-augmented generation platform
candidates.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have transformed knowledge discovery, but their use in sensitive domains is limited by privacy concerns and risks of data leakage. Moreover, LLMs may hallucinate when queried about information outside their training data, undermining their reliability for scientific, clinical, or policy-related tasks. We present MyGPT, a fully open-source, privacy-preserving retrieval-augmented-generation (RAG) platform that uses open-source LLMs and operates locally or within secure institutional environments. MyGPT empowers users to query user-defined libraries such as biomedical literature, confidential clinical documents, and multilingual global health policies, while ensuring that sensitive data never leaves the secure environment. We introduce confidence metrics, including “relevance scores” and “hallucination index,” and provide explicit source citation from the library within a single interface to assess contextual support for generated answers. MyGPT offers a cost-effective, modular, open-source alternative to commercial LLM services and democratizes knowledge-seeking across multiple domains, including use at remote facilities without internet access.

candidates.title: Improving Reliability of Retrieval-Augmented Generation by Detecting and Correcting Irrelevant Retrieved Context
candidates.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) lets a language model answer from external documents instead of relying on its parameters alone, yet the answer can be no more dependable than the passages placed in its prompt. Retrievers rank by similarity, and similarity is not the same as usefulness: passages that share vocabulary or subject matter with a query frequently lack the evidence it needs, and a generator may still follow them. This paper reviews three recent lines of work that attack RAG reliability from different directions—corrective retrieval (CRAG), a word-level hallucination corpus (RAGTruth) and counterfactual risk control—and compares what each does before, during and after generation. Using their published results, we show that judging retrieval quality ahead of generation brings large gains, whereas detection and abstention methods only guard the output once the context is already fixed. Building on this analysis we outline a pre-generation framework that scores every retrieved chunk, separates relevant, partially relevant, irrelevant and insufficient evidence, refines or re-retrieves within a bounded budget, and abstains when evidence stays inadequate. A latency model and an evaluation protocol for testing the framework are provided. The paper closes with open problems in evaluator accuracy, cost and cross-domain robustness.

candidates.title: Image-Based Dietary Assessment Using Multimodal Large Language Models: Performance, Limitations, and Clinical Applicability in Diabetes
candidates.abstract: Background Image-based dietary assessment is useful for precision diabetes care. Multimodal Large Language Models (mLLMs) may greatly facilitate dietary self-monitoring. However, comprehensive evaluation of their real-world accuracy remains limited. Methods We developed SeeFood, an open-source benchmark, and evaluated eight commercial and open-source mLLMs on 80 real-world meal photographs from the SNAPMe dataset for nutrient and energy estimation (calories, carbohydrates, protein, fat, fiber), food-item identification, and day-level diet quality (Healthy Eating Index, HEI-2020). Three finalists were evaluated on the complete dataset (1680 photographs, 275 participant-days), and the best model was analyzed by meal type, portion size, sizing-marker use, ingredient visibility and meal complexity. Results GPT-4o mini achieved the lowest errors, with a significant advantage for carbohydrates; the three finalists performed similarly on other outcomes and on HEI-2020. Mean absolute percentage errors (MAPE) remained high (52%--90%), and the direction of bias was model-specific. The carbohydrate mean absolute error was 13.3 g (95% CI 12.4--14.3), and only 57% of meals were within +/- 10 g, a clinically relevant threshold for insulin dosing in type 1 diabetes. Calorie errors for lunch and dinner were in the range reported for human estimation on other images (~55% MAPE), whereas drink-only images had the highest relative errors (312% MAPE) because of dissolved sugars. Food items were reliably identified when fully visible (Dice = 0.74), and HEI-2020 estimates showed moderate agreement with reference values (RMSE = 12.5 points; r = 0.61). Larger portions were increasingly underestimated, and sizing references did not improve accuracy. Newer or larger models and chain-of-thought prompting did not consistently improve performance. Conclusions Current mLLMs can extract meaningful dietary information from real-world meal photographs, but substantial errors in nutrient and portion-size estimation currently limit their use for precision diabetes management. Integrating visual assessment with additional contextual information may enable more reliable, lower-burden dietary monitoring.

candidates.title: ADAPTIVE MULTIMODAL RETRIEVAL-AUGMENTED GENERATION WITH CONTEXT-AWARE HALLUCINATION DETECTION FOR RELIABLE KNOWLEDGE SYSTEMS
candidates.abstract: This paper investigates adaptive retrieval and hallucination detection in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems using independently verified data. It develops a knowledge corpus of 44 arXiv abstracts, 108 questions, and a synthetic benchmark of 432 labelled examples to evaluate TF-IDF, BM25, and Latent Semantic Analysis (LSA) retrieval methods. TF-IDF achieves the highest Recall@1 (94.4%), while Gradient Boosting performs best in hallucination detection, with an F1-score of 0.962 and ROC-AUC of 0.982. The results reveal that retrieving additional passages can increase ungrounded answers due to distractor passages. Furthermore, the detector trained on synthetic data struggles to identify real pipeline failures, highlighting the impact of distribution shift. An adaptive retrieval strategy based on detector confidence achieves comparable groundedness to an oracle retrieval policy while expanding the context for only 11.1% of questions. A supplementary cross-modal experiment demonstrates promising text-to-image retrieval performance. The study provides a reproducible framework for evaluating adaptive retrieval, hallucination detection, and multimodal retrieval in RAG systems.

candidates.title: The LLENS Platform for On-Premises Large Language Model Agents in a Japanese University Hospital: Development and Evaluation Study
candidates.abstract: Large language model agents that use tools could take on part of the electronic health record and desk work that occupies physicians' time, but in many hospitals the medical information systems run inside closed networks, so the model and the agent harness must also sit inside. We designed, implemented, and deployed LLENS, a clinical support AI agent platform that runs inside the closed network of Hokkaido University Hospital on one host with 8 NVIDIA H200 GPUs, the open-weight model Kimi K2.6 (~1 trillion parameters), and a web application rebuilt from Open WebUI. The harness has 10 components, including page image reading, full-text attachment input, a path-addressed document tree without a vector index, a network-isolated sandbox, artifact return, self-checking of generated output, subagents, and saved procedures. Kimi K2.6 was chosen from 3 open-weight candidates and scored 480/500 on the 2026 Japanese Medical Licensing Examination; it generated 119 tokens/s for one user and served 16 concurrent requests at 908 tokens/s in total. On 180 questions over hospital documents (3 seeds each), mean accuracy was 10.7% with no documents, 81.3% with fixed retrieval (top 10 chunks of one lexical search), and 97.2% with interactive access, in which the model reads with document tools and the sandbox (15.9 percentage points above fixed retrieval, 95% CI 10.9-21.3); the difference lay in filtering/counting questions (16.7% vs 87.8%). Five scenarios with synthetic data ran on combinations of the components: needlestick injury response, batch adverse event grading, scanned referral letter transcription, falls data aggregation and plotting, and investigation of 3 topics by subagents. The platform has run on the hospital network since September 14, 2026.

candidates.title: On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: On-policy self-distillation enables post-training foundation models without relying on stronger external teachers. However, existing approaches rely on ground-truth question-answer pairs, human-curated problem sets, or other supervised signals. In this work, we reformulate on-policy self-distillation as a self-training framework, driven by self-generated question-answer pairs and privileged reasoning demonstrations. We push supervision to the limit: guided solely by coarse, high-level topic descriptions, the model synthesizes its own curriculum of queries and privileged reasoning traces without access to any human-curated prompts or answers. We find that self-distillation on fully synthetic privileged information enables a model to improve across multiple domains while retaining its capabilities on domains it is not self-trained on. We demonstrate the generality of this framework across text and multimodal domains, achieving consistent self-improvement on standard language benchmarks and Visual Question Answering. Our findings demonstrate that foundation models possess rich latent capabilities that can be amplified without external task supervision or curated problem distributions.

candidates.title: Retrieval-augmented generation in biomedicine: a survey of technologies, datasets, and clinical applications
candidates.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) in biomedicine face a fundamental conflict between static parameter knowledge and the dynamic nature of clinical evidence. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) addresses this by grounding generation in external data, yet it introduces new complexities in latency and architecture. This survey synthesizes the biomedical RAG landscape from 2020 to 2025 through a structured literature mapping of 178 screened records, yielding 94 representative studies classified into naive RAG (38 studies, 40.4%), advanced RAG (46 studies, 48.9%), and modular RAG (10 studies, 10.7%). Beyond a technological taxonomy, we formalize the biomedical RAG trilemma, identifying the inherent trade-offs between reasoning depth, inference latency, and data privacy that constrain current clinical deployment. We analyze how recent agentic workflows enhance diagnostic reasoning but risk prohibitive latency, and how privacy constraints dictate the choice between powerful cloud-based models and local deployment. Finally, we outline the alignment gap in multimodal RAG and propose future directions for self-correcting, verifiable clinical agents.

candidates.title: NgramRL: Accelerating RL Post-Training for Structured Generation via Rollout-Aware N-gram Speculative Decoding
candidates.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training improves the reasoning capabilities of large language models, but its cost is dominated by autoregressive rollout generation, which can exceed 70% of training time. Existing speculative-decoding methods are poorly suited to this setting: model-based drafters consume scarce GPU memory and may become misaligned as the policy evolves, while existing model-free methods do not explicitly exploit repetition across training epochs. We observe that recent rollouts of the same prompt provide a high-quality, self-updating draft source. Based on this insight, we propose NgramRL, a per-prompt n-gram drafter constructed from bounded recent rollout history. NgramRL requires no auxiliary model, drafter training, or persistent GPU-resident drafter state, while target-model verification preserves the rollout distribution. To hide CPU cache lookup and scheduling, we further introduce an adaptive fan-out prefetcher that predicts likely verification outcomes (j, b), consisting of the accepted draft length j and target-emitted continuation token b. A causal budget allocator concentrates prefetches on high-probability outcomes, while uncovered outcomes fall back to sequential lookup without changing committed tokens. Across two model families and three reasoning and structured-generation workloads, NgramRL commits 3.60-7.77 tokens per target-model forward in the warm-cache regime, up to 1.99x more than SuffixDecoding and 7.0x more than prompt-lookup decoding. On Spider, the prefetcher covers 96.6% of Qwen3-8B outcomes at a candidate budget of 16 and improves measured rollout throughput by 1.38x over synchronous NgramRL, approaching its 1.40x overlap ceiling.

candidates.title: MPQ: A Message-Passing View of Post-Training Quantization
candidates.abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) is a key technique for efficiently deploying large language models, as it compresses weights into low-bit representations without retraining. Existing PTQ solvers, including GPTQ, LDLQ, and block coordinate descent, commit each weight block to a single codeword before its neighbors are considered, leaving near-optimal alternatives unexplored. In this work, we cast row-wise PTQ as posterior inference over discrete codebooks, in which existing solvers correspond to a zero-temperature, hard-decision limit retaining only the top codeword per block. We propose Message-Passing Quantization (MPQ), which preserves soft posterior information across blocks during inference and commits to hard codewords only at the output stage. MPQ first uses vector approximate message passing to compute approximate blockwise posteriors, then refines a hard-decision initialization by exact block coordinate descent. Across 2-bit lattice and 3- and 4-bit scalar quantization on dense language models from Llama, Qwen, and Mistral families, MPQ improves perplexity and zero-shot accuracy over strong hard-decision baselines, and composes favorably with preprocessing techniques such as activation-aware scaling and incoherence processing. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/poseidonchan/MPQ.

candidates.title: BiLoCo: Binary Low-Rank Corrections for Post-Training Quantization
candidates.abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) to FP4 has emerged as a key technique for reducing large language model inference cost, especially on Blackwell GPUs, which offer native FP4 tensor core support. Direct PTQ to FP4, however, still leaves a noticeable accuracy gap. Recent work on SVDQuant mitigates the errors introduced through FP4 quantization for diffusion models by adding high-precision low-rank corrections obtained via SVD. However, this high-precision low-rank correction requires many bits per rank, and it runs on the same tensor cores as the main FP4 GEMM. We introduce BiLoCo, a low-rank correction method whose left and right factors are stored as binary ${\{\pm 1\}}$ sign vectors rather than as BF16 numbers. The signed format uses $16{\times}$ less storage per rank-one component, and since the correction now consists of additions/subtractions, this can be run on CUDA cores concurrently with the FP4 tensor-core GEMM. On 4B--72B LLMs, BiLoCo matches or improves memory-matched SVDQuant for PTQ. We implement BiLoCo on B300 as a fused single kernel, where the FP4 GEMM runs on tensor cores, the bit-packed correction on the CUDA cores of the same launch, and the two are combined in the GEMM epilogue. With batch size $1$, the fused kernel is at most $11\%$ slower than the FP4-only GEMM for every rank up to $512$. At rank $128$, it is at most $20\%$ slower up to batch size $8$.

candidates.title: In RAG We Trust? Measuring Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Under Post-Retrieval Context Tampering
candidates.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation grounds a language model in retrieved documents, and that grounding is also an attack surface: an adversary who edits retrieved text, without touching the model or the retriever, can feed the model fluent falsehoods. We measure this on a 4-bit Llama 3.1 8B system with a MiniLM retriever over FEVER evidence. This version replaces the measurement rather than reinterpreting it. The earlier sweep contained an off-by-one that made a zero-corruption cell impossible, so the row published as a clean baseline carried one corrupted passage; a seeded re-run of 1,911 generations supplies a real control, logs how many passages each corruption rule actually modified, and adds closed-book and irrelevant-context arms. Three results follow. Scored on corruption actually applied, the fooled rate runs 0.4%, 35.7%, 54.0% and 72.0% for zero through three corrupted passages, the zero cell being an internal control with no adoption at all. The rules do not deliver the corruption they request: asked for three passages, numeric substitution achieves it in 6% of cells, so the three rules were never comparable and we withdraw the ranking we previously published. Controls reframe the rest, since the generator is more accurate with no context (83.7%) than with clean retrieved context (77.6%), and with irrelevant context it abstains on every question rather than using knowledge it demonstrably has.

candidates.title: Autonomous Agents Based on Large Language Models: Reasoning Strategies and Multi-Agent Interaction
candidates.abstract: Language-model agents acquire capability along two routes that published work almost always varies together, one enlarging the computation a single agent performs and the other enlarging the number of agents and the channels along which they pass partial results, which leaves the contribution of each route indistinguishable. This paper separates an agent system into a reasoning operator and an interaction topology, holding the number of agents fixed at three across all multi-agent topologies, together with the number of rounds, the message cap, the prompt skeleton, and the memory settings for all combinations, and evaluates a full factorial design of four reasoning levels and four topologies on three public test sets totalling 484 instances under five random seeds, giving 38,720 task executions. Comparisons are paired at the instance level, and effects are estimated from logistic mixed-effects models fitted to each test set separately. The reasoning factor spans 18.0 points on the static suite whereas the topology factor spans 7.8 points on the interactive one, a reversal indicating that the two mechanisms act on different failure modes. The topology span is taken across all four topology levels and therefore includes the step from one agent to three, against a structure-only span of 2.8 points among the multi-agent topologies. The two factors also depart from additivity in a localised manner. A mechanism-motivated single-degree-of-freedom contrast on the only cell in which both factors contribute a corrective pass is significant at p = 0.001 on the static suite, whereas the omnibus nine-degree-of-freedom interaction test is not (p = 0.094), and in that cell the observed 50.0 percent lies 5.8 points below the additive expectation. After tokens are counted, seven of the sixteen configurations remain undominated on the static suite and five on the operating-system suite, and returns saturate at 12,400 tokens per instance on the static suite under the present design.

candidates.title: Using Large Language Models in Your PhD
candidates.abstract: This chapter explains how PhD students can use large language models (LLMs) to support research without outsourcing scholarship. It covers practical uses in writing, literature exploration, coding, experiment planning, and self-critique, while emphasizing that you remain responsible for accuracy, reasoning, and originality. The chapter highlights common failure modes such as fabricated citations, confident errors, and overly agreeable “reviews,” and discusses when LLM feedback is helpful versus misleading. It also outlines responsible use, including disclosure norms, bias awareness, and protecting confidential data. The goal is to benefit from speed and breadth while staying intellectually in control.

candidates.title: Solvent: Long-Horizon Reasoning for Multi-Step Retrosynthesis
candidates.abstract: Multi-step retrosynthesis requires recursively transforming a target molecule through successive reaction steps into purchasable building blocks, and recent work has begun to draw on large language model (LLM) reasoning to tackle the task. In its latest evolution, LLM reasoning has entered the long-horizon regime: models pursue objectives across interdependent steps, interact with environments, and adapt to feedback. This shift has markedly advanced LLM capabilities, as illustrated by breakthroughs in AI-driven mathematical research. At this frontier, we introduce Solvent, an 8B LLM that successfully extends long-horizon reasoning to multi-step retrosynthesis. Through a two-round post-training curriculum, Solvent learns to interleave iterative synthesis planning, external availability verification, and adaptive route revision. Experiments show that, following a $2.1\times$ performance boost from RL, Solvent scores 61.86% across four benchmarks, surpassing mid-scale language models and prior search-based retrosynthesis systems, and rivaling frontier trillion-parameter LLMs.

candidates.title: Sharpness-aware Orthogonalized Momentum Algorithms
candidates.abstract: Adversarial sharpness penalty per iteration of a base optimizer, known as sharpness-aware minimization (SAM), is an accepted technique to improve generalization in deep learning. Recently, Muon has emerged as a dominant optimization algorithm for training large language models (LLMs). It achieves lower sample complexity for heavy-tailed gradient updates - a phenomenon common in LLM training. However, sharpness penalties with Muon updates are yet largely unexplored in the literature. Moreover, the behavior of SAM under heavy-tailed noise is unknown both theoretically and empirically. A potential reason for this gap is the additional cost of extra gradient computation per iteration for penalty perturbations in SAM, which becomes prohibitive for LLMs. This paper introduces Sharpness-aware Orthogonalized Momentum Algorithm (SOMA) to combine a computationally efficient and theoretically grounded perturbation scheme with the Muon algorithm. The key idea is to use stale (purely) stochastic gradient noise for adversarial perturbations. Theoretically, we show that SOMA's sample complexity is invariant to the perturbation direction. We provide explorations and insights into SOMA's robustness to heavy-tailed gradient noise. We extensively explore SOMA's efficacy in (a) mitigating quality degradation due to post-training quantization, and (b) catastrophic forgetting during fine-tuning of LLMs.

candidates.title: Permission Withdrawal in Tool-Using Language Model Agents: Runtime Enforcement and Recovery
candidates.abstract: AI agents that operate external tools can continue acting after a user narrows their permissions, creating a security problem that final-state evaluation may fail to detect. Existing agent benchmarks commonly emphasize task completion or resulting state, but those outcomes do not reveal whether an unauthorized operation was proposed, approved, dispatched, or merely prevented by a downstream error. We investigate permission withdrawal as a trajectory-level authorization problem and evaluate whether runtime gates can preserve revised permissions while allowing agents to complete work that remains authorized. Two acting models were tested in a deterministic tool environment under prompt-only execution, a rule-based reference gate, and a model-based gate. A 72-episode diagnostic examined two previously exposed write workflows, followed by a separately frozen 384-episode extension spanning eight new tasks and four authorization mechanisms. In the diagnostic, prompt-only agents executed forbidden same-value writes in two episodes; both runtime gates prevented forbidden execution, although the model gate falsely rejected three authorized calls. In the extension, 346 of 384 episodes completed safely and 383 preserved the required protected state. No forbidden request executed successfully, yet the model gate approved three unauthorized requests that were stopped only because the referenced resources did not exist. The results demonstrate that correct final state and zero forbidden execution can still conceal failures in authorization reasoning. We contribute a replayable evaluation framework that separates proposals, gate decisions, dispatch, state transitions, and useful completion, enabling more precise assessment of security controls for tool-using agents.

candidates.title: PRISM: Promoting Sampling Diversity of Large Language Models with Implicit Stochastic Modulation
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) exhibit mode collapse, where their output distribution concentrates on familiar semantic modes. When diversity disappears, repeated sampling becomes semantic repetition rather than discovery, making rare but stronger solutions unlikely to surface and leaving self-evolution and continual learning difficult to sustain. Most remedies intervene only at inference time, shaping sam- ples without making diversity a model capability. We propose PRISM, a training-time framework that internalizes diversity within the model. PRISM combines (i) submodular curation that pairs each prompt with diverse-yet-correct multi-teacher solutions, and (ii) stochastic embedding modulation, which turns special-token perturbations into implicit signals for sampling distinct outputs. A theoretical analysis establishes the stability of this mechanism. On WritingPrompts and BookMIA, PRISM moves the quality-diversity frontier outward, achieving the best generation quality in all model-benchmark settings while maintaining the strongest or near-strongest semantic diversity across two open-weight model families. It also improves sampling efficiency on math and code benchmarks. Beyond inference, PRISM yields a stronger foundation for reinforcement learning, sustaining diverse rollouts and mitigating the diversity collapse commonly observed during RL training.

candidates.title: LeafSkill: Efficient Leaf-Level Action Grounding for Recursive LLM Agents
candidates.abstract: Recursive large language model (LLM) agents solve long-horizon tasks through decomposition, execution, and environmental feedback. Yet after producing an atomic subtask, they often invoke the same large model again to translate a familiar instruction into an executable action. We observe that high-level planning is task-specific, whereas leaf-level action grounding recurs across tasks and can be checked against environment-admitted actions. We introduce LeafSkill, an external reuse layer that retrieves semantically related grounding experience, binds action templates to current objects and admissible actions, and uses a lightweight 1.7B selector to choose a bound action or defer the unchanged subtask to the original agent. Skills remain outside the model parameters, allowing a frozen selector to use post-training additions. Under lexical and syntactic paraphrases, exact matching retrieves none of the reference actions, while semantic retrieval preserves 96.0% and 97.0% candidate coverage; the frozen selector adopts 97.34% of unseen skill types. On an independent confirmation set of 200 Robotouille tasks, LeafSkill completes 137 tasks versus 121 for ReCAP (68.5% vs. 60.5%, exact McNemar p=.0259). On the 106 tasks completed by both, it reduces Qwen3.5-27B tokens by 14.42% and calls by 14.08%. A separate held-out repeat yields a consistent 9.0-point success gain and 18.98% token reduction. Reusable leaf grounding can thus improve task completion while reducing host-model inference without replacing high-level planning.

candidates.title: LLaCO: Continuous Diffusion for Large Language Models with Competition-Aware Semantic Scheduling
candidates.abstract: Continuous diffusion models have emerged as a promising non-autoregressive paradigm for text generation over continuous embedding spaces. Along the continuous trajectory, the residual token identity directly shapes the denoising objective. However, the geometric trajectory misaligns with temporal progression, triggering severe temporal compression. In this paper, we show that embedding norm decay causes Euclidean distance to yield spurious overtaking, indicating that token competition must be evaluated directionally. In this space, a candidate overtakes the source token only when the effective noise magnitude surpasses their semantic separation. We formalize these pairwise dynamics as the Competition Threshold Theory (CTT). Crucially, high-dimensional overtaking requires extreme noise levels, causing standard trajectories to concentrate identity decay into a narrow window near the noisy endpoint. To resolve this, we propose Semantic Retention Scheduling (SRS) to align time allocation with the progression of identity decay, and demonstrate that existing token identity metrics are fundamentally statistical aggregations of these pairwise crossings. Building on these theoretical insights, we introduce LLaCO, a generative framework powered by competition-aware semantic scheduling. LLaCO adapts a pretrained backbone to continuous representations via an embedding directional adapter and timestep-conditioned modulation. To operate within the directional space, LLaCO employs a spherical noising process formulated as a geodesic interpolation toward a mask-biased endpoint, eliminating norm decay while preserving accurate token competition. Guided by SRS, LLaCO reallocates the denoising trajectory proportionally to the logarithmic rank decay. Instantiated as an 8B model, LLaCO outperforms previous continuous diffusion baselines and rivals discrete diffusion models of comparable scale.

candidates.title: From archive to resource: bringing legacy data back to life at scale with large language models
candidates.abstract: Pharmaceutical companies maintain vast archives of legacy preclinical study reports that contain study-context details, such as fasting, anesthesia, and laboratory instrumentation, that are rarely captured in structured data formats, yet they can correlate with clinical pathology parameters values and limit the reuse of historical data. This work demonstrates practical, scalable solutions to recover such descriptors from heterogeneous report texts using large language model (LLM)-based extraction pipelines developed independently by two industry teams. The pipelines identify and normalize metadata fields and return verbatim evidence with page and section reference, hasting human verification and iterative refinement. Evaluation of over 400 documents against expert-curated reference values showed high agreement across a broad set of metadata fields. Performance was strongest for consistently reported items and lower for descriptors subject to linguistic or report structure variability. Extraction time has shrunk from 25 minutes in the manual benchmark to 1.6 minutes. As a concrete biological demonstration, we show that fasting status extracted from report text was associated with species- and analyte-specific shifts in clinical chemistry parameters, illustrating how recovered metadata can improve selection of historical controls. Key strengths of the approach are scalability, traceability, and the ability to recover information missing from current industry standards. Main limitations are dependence on source-report quality and initial expert effort to define and refine schemas. These results establish how LLMs can convert heterogeneous, unstructured legacy reports into evidence-grounded, reusable and structured metadata, leading to better experimental comparability, and thus enabling reliable data pooling or informed virtual control selection.

candidates.title: Every Edge Needs a Quote: Building a Quote-Grounded Knowledge Graph of Healthcare Software Adoption with Language-Model Agents
candidates.abstract: Hospitals regularly buy software that clinicians and patients depend on. Because these purchases are costly, hard to reverse and can affect patient care, buyers look for evidence of which peer institutions already use a product and which systems it connects to. This evidence is public but scattered across vendor websites, press releases and third-party pages. Language-model agents can now collect it at low cost, but the correctness of the extracted claims is difficult to establish, and a wrongly listed customer can mislead buyers and misrepresent an organisation. We present a pipeline that builds a knowledge graph of customer and integration relations from the open web under one rule: every edge must be supported by a verbatim quote from its source page. Pages come from a deterministic crawl of each vendor's site and a budgeted ReAct agent that searches the rest of the web. A permissive extractor proposes relations with quotes, and a layered grounding stage decides which to keep, using a referent step that reads the whole page when a quote names only one side, deterministic checks, and a panel of five model calls voting on nine criteria. On 61 vendors, the pipeline reaches 0.94 precision and 0.71 recall against a page-level key covering the 6,428 candidate relations proposed by its extractor, whose verdicts were drafted by one model and re-checked with a second. Against the golden reference, the marketplace's own curated list, it scores lower, but 89% of the relations it keeps that the reference lacks are stated on a page. A confidence score built from the panel's votes keeps more correct relations than the fixed rule at the same precision, and reaches 0.90 precision at 0.90 recall. We also discuss how narrow, bounded model calls, string-matched evidence and voting address long-context degradation and run-to-run variance.

candidates.title: Behaviour analysis for large language model-driven agents
candidates.abstract: Understanding language-agent behaviour requires learning how actions are organised across a trajectory and how this organisation relates to context and outcomes. We propose a general framework that connects data-driven behavioural discovery with analysis and experimental investigation. Categories developed from recorded activity define what is measured. Analyses preserve the behaviours' positions in the process and express their relationships as interpretable hypotheses. Statistical assessment and tests in held-out contexts examine the strength and scope of the evidence. Experiments, including prompt steering, then test how behaviour and outcomes change under deliberately varied conditions. A study of iterative self-reflection illustrates how discovery, dependency learning and prompt comparisons can inform one another. We develop this approach for trajectories of varying length, event order and agent roles, and identify advances in coding, analysis and experimentation needed to support its wider use.

candidates.title: Profile-Driven User Simulation via Reinforcement Learning with Hierarchical Rewards for Task-Oriented Dialogues
candidates.abstract: Building Task-Oriented Dialogue (TOD) systems for high-value scenarios such as financial marketing requires large volumes of domain-specific dialogue data, which privacy regulations, annotation costs, and the need for expert labor make hard to obtain. User simulation offers a remedy, but existing methods target general-domain dialogue and exhibit two key limitations: insufficient modeling of domain-specific business processes and compliance constraints, and inadequate capture of the colloquial, spoken-language character of voice interactions. We propose ProfileSim, a profile-driven user simulation framework for financial marketing outbound calls. It jointly models user profiles---demographics and Big Five personality traits---and business profiles---intents reverse-engineered from real call logs---enabling fine-grained control over simulated behavior. The base model is fine-tuned on real voice dialogue data and refined by Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with hierarchical rewards at the dialogue and utterance levels. Paired with a customer service agent integrating Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) constraints and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), ProfileSim achieves the highest colloquial naturalness, the strongest user profile adherence and the lowest agent score on long-tail intents among all evaluated user generators, while producing substantially shorter user utterances at comparable business compliance. The generated dialogue data is designed to support intent recognition training, agent evaluation, and rapid cold-start deployment.

candidates.title: Guess Close, Search Exact: A Formally Verified, Model-Free Memory and Mutation Engine for Language-Model Agents
candidates.abstract: Language models are good at proposing roughly right answers and poor at being exactly right, cheaply, every time. neo4d is a model-free engine that sits beside a model: it mutates code token by token and lets the tests judge every variant, searches the neighbourhood of a model's attempt, and remembers verified work as placeholder plans it can replay without the model. What it trusts is decided by RELATE v2, an eight-bit integer law with no branches, checked on all 2^32 inputs for undefined behaviour (UBSan, CBMC); its nine principles hold on every reachable input and eight further properties on all 256 eight-bit inputs. Under a teacher that gives 10% wrong lessons, the law keeps 58.4% of what memory produces correct, against 0.9% when every pattern is trusted at first sight and 1.7% without its barren rule, at equal coverage. With neo4d, phi4-mini fixes 62.5% of 176 bugs (30.7% alone, 42.0% with three tries) and completes 47.1% of 85 multi-step agent tasks (25.9% alone, 40.0% with three tries) with fewer calls. Claude Sonnet and Claude Haiku keep their accuracy (85/85, 84/85) while neo4d takes 32% and 40% of the tasks off them; a replayed plan takes 0.59 s against 20-36 s for a model. With Haiku only choosing which branches to explore, neo4d's search fixes 17 hard two-fault bugs where a blind search fixes 14 and a random filter 12.0, with 60% fewer test runs. On real bugs at an equal budget over three seeds, a loop in which neo4d mutates each of the model's attempts fixes 24.7 of 31 with gemma3:4b against 16.0-18.7 for sample-and-filter, self-debugging and Reflexion (p <= 0.016) with about 35% fewer calls; with phi4-mini it leads (23.0 against 20.0-22.3) without a significant difference. On two domains that are not code - a numbers puzzle and block-stacking plans - the same core, unchanged, lifts both small models far above their own methods (Countdown: from 0 to 26-31 of 40), but its search alone, with no model, does as well or better: there the small models' guesses are worse starts than a neutral one. Negative results are reported equally: evidence handed to a small model as a paragraph made it worse, marks on suspect lines helped one model and hurt another, and nothing helped on bugs a strong model already solves. Implementation, experiments and text were produced with Claude Code (Anthropic) under the author's direction. Code, results and every run: https://github.com/devkancheti4-design/neo4d. SWE-bench results will follow in a later version.

candidates.title: 4DMemory: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Spatiotemporal Memory with Harness-Augmented Agents
candidates.abstract: Humans efficiently process multimodal streams spanning hours to years, building persistent, fine-grained spatiotemporal memories that support reasoning about and predicting long-horizon events. In contrast, existing benchmarks focus on short- and medium-context tasks, and most foundation models struggle to preserve fine-grained information over long horizons. To evaluate and improve long-horizon spatiotemporal reasoning, we introduce the LongVideo dataset and the 4DMemoryBench. LongVideo comprises about 900 hours of video and over 5,000 manually reviewed questions covering visual, textual, and spatiotemporal reasoning across diverse context lengths. We further develop the 4DMemory Harness, which integrates four complementary skills, 22+ specialized tool models, and a model-specific retrieval-augmented generation system. Evaluating 13 leading models, we find that standalone foundation models struggle with long-horizon tasks, while the 4DMemory Harness improves all of them by over 50\%. Compared to previous benchmark, the same models exhibit a performance drop of more than 10\% on 4DMemoryBench. We hope 4DMemory will facilitate the development of spatiotemporal agents capable of addressing complex, long-horizon tasks.

candidates.title: Where Rounding Happens Matters: Rounding-Location Alignment Stabilizes LLM Reinforcement Learning
candidates.abstract: Reinforcement learning for large language models often uses separate systems for inference and training. Even with identical weights and BF16 tensors, implementation differences can make an intended on-policy update off-policy and destabilize training. Existing remedies align the entire inference and training stacks, change global precision, or modify the learning algorithm. We ask whether aligning selected parts of the execution stack can stabilize BF16 RL while other implementation differences remain. We align training-side rounding locations with inference in three regions---RoPE, SwiGLU, and residual RMSNorm---by retaining selected intermediates in FP32 until their BF16 outputs. Across four Qwen-family models, aligning all three regions prevents the collapse observed under the default BF16 baseline; RoPE-path alignment alone also suffices in the studied runs, despite remaining numerical discrepancies. The interventions keep the inference engine, matrix-multiplication and attention kernels, and learning objective unchanged.

candidates.title: Trusting the Tool: Asymmetric Deference of LLM Vulnerability Auditors to Static-Analysis Evidence
candidates.abstract: Pipelines that combine large language models (LLMs) with static analysis let the model consume the analyser's output as evidence, but whether the model distinguishes true from false evidence, and whether its scrutiny depends on what the evidence claims, has not been measured. We built an intraprocedural analyser for C/C++ that produces proof obligations and audited vulnerable and patched functions from PrimeVul under six evidence conditions that differ only in the notes, including fabricated assurances that a missing check exists and fabricated alarms that an added check is missing. The study covers 916 pairs in four disjoint sets, eleven model configurations from four vendors and 16,572 audits; no model is trained or fine-tuned. True evidence barely improved accuracy (+0.02). False evidence acted asymmetrically: relative to true notes about the same operations, false assurances lowered the detection of real vulnerabilities by up to 19 points, whereas false alarms never significantly lowered accuracy and were disputed far more often. An internally registered replication on seven new models confirmed that false assurances move verdicts towards their claim more than false alarms do (mean asymmetry +0.16, 95% CI +0.10 to +0.24). Instructions in the audit prompt did not reliably reduce deference; the best one failed to replicate. Verifying each claim in a separate call and showing the refuted claims raised accuracy under false assurances by 12 points in a pre-specified test (p=0.002) without loss under true evidence; for a second model the gain was smaller and not significant. Pipelines should therefore verify a tool's guarantees before the model relies on them, and studies should measure deference in a direction-aware way.

candidates.title: Training an MoE LLM in MXFP4: How We Closed the Gap to BF16
candidates.abstract: Training large language models (LLMs) in sub-8-bit arithmetic promises substantial gains in memory bandwidth and compute throughput, yet FP4 formats introduce quantization error severe enough to destabilize optimization if left unaddressed. We present ALTO, an open-source training recipe for GPT-OSS-20B, a 20-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model, on the MLPerf Small MoE Training benchmark under the MXFP4 microscaling format. The recipe combines established techniques from Abecassis, Felix et al. [arXiv:2509.25149] (hybrid 1D/2D block quantization, randomized Hadamard transforms, and stochastic rounding) with a simplified weight de-oscillation scheme adapted from TetraJet-v2 [arXiv:2510.27527]. On C4 validation at global batch size 16, MXFP4 + RHT + SR + de-oscillation reaches a validation loss of 3.3350 at 16,128 steps, only 0.007 above the BF16 baseline (3.3283), closing roughly 50% of the gap left by MXFP4 without de-oscillation (3.3418). Measured by steps to reach the MLPerf quality target (validation loss 3.34), de-oscillation cuts the FP4 convergence overhead relative to BF16 from +20.0% to +5.0%. We also report negative end-to-end results from differential gradient estimation, outlier clipping, and macro-block scaling, despite each showing operator-level SNR gains. All experiments use simulated MXFP4 kernels on AMD MI300 hardware and wall-clock speed has not been optimized.

candidates.title: The Butterfly Defects: Tracing Cooperation in LLM Agent Networks
candidates.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) increasingly operate as interconnected agents, a fundamental question emerges: does individual cooperation translate into collective cooperation? We investigate this question through the Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma (IPD), moving from dyadic interactions to homogeneous and heterogeneous networks of open-weight LLMs. Our findings reveal that cooperation is highly sensitive to model composition and seemingly minor linguistic changes. Models that cooperate with identical peers can shift toward defection in mixed populations. A simple uncertainty cue can increase or decrease cooperation, redistribute costs, and affect unexposed agents several hops away. Even reversing action-label order can dramatically alter behavior, with uncertainty framing sometimes amplifying this sensitivity. Together, these findings challenge the notion of cooperation as a stable model-level property, revealing how strategic behavior depends on interaction partners, network positions, and the language used to frame decisions.

candidates.title: TGR-EvoDAG: A DAG-based Multi-Agent Code Evolution Framework for Generative Recommendation on Tencent
candidates.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents have enabled automated code evolution for algorithm discovery. However, current recursive self-improvement (RSI) research for sequential recommendation faces a dilemma: general-purpose frameworks lack domain-specific feedback, while recommender-specific frameworks rely on linear evolution. Crucially, naively integrating them fails when applied to Generative Recommendation (GR). Unlike end-to-end models, GR relies on a module-cascaded pipeline (tokenization, pre-training, and alignment). In this paradigm, existing evolution methods suffer from: i) cost blindness, squandering budgets by ignoring stage-asymmetric retraining overheads; and ii) short-sighted evaluation, discarding promising upstream innovations that temporarily regress metrics before downstream adaptation. To bridge these gaps, we propose TGR-EvoDAG, a multi-agent code evolution framework tailored for GR. TGR-EvoDAG models code evolution as a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) to maintain multiple evolution branches and merge complementary innovations, unifying advanced search with rich GR diagnostic feedback. We further introduce stage-aware cost planning to optimize GPU-hour budgets, and active downstream co-adaptation to navigate temporary regressions and unlock cross-stage gains. On public Amazon datasets, TGR-EvoDAG enables the first autonomous evolution of a complete GR pipeline, improving offline metrics by up to 37.4% and Agent4Rec simulated user satisfaction by 19.7% over the strongest baseline. Furthermore, in industrial deployment on Tencent's large-scale commercial media platform, the evolved GR achieves a 12.16% relative improvement in offline Hit@1 and a statistically significant 0.40% increase in online click-through rate (CTR).

candidates.title: SOPO: Socratic Guided Policy Optimization for Span-Level Hallucination Detection
candidates.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have gained widespread adoption in various natural language processing tasks, but suffer from hallucination issues where they generate unfaithful or inconsistent content. While Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has shown promising applications in reasoning tasks, its application to span-level hallucination detection is challenged by localization ambiguity, reward sparsity on hard examples, and uncontrolled length inflation. To address these issues, we introduce Socratic Guided Policy Optimization (SOPO), a multi-turn RL framework for robust hallucination detection. The key innovation of SOPO is a Socratic feedback mechanism, where a teacher model guides the reasoning trajectories during rollout by providing indirect hints inferred from the ground truth. This teacher-guided approach enables the model to generate more effective reasoning trajectories for hard examples, thus alleviating reward sparsity. Furthermore, we incorporate Turn-based Advantage Scaling to penalize verbosity bias, encouraging the model to develop efficient and autonomous reasoning capabilities. candidates.title: SCI-AGENT-EXAM: Benchmarking Agents on Scientific Research Tasks
candidates.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly capable of supporting scientific workflows, but their capabilities across diverse research activities remain difficult to assess systematically. Each task requires both executable artifacts (e.g., code and scripts) and textual artifacts (e.g., reports and explanations). To evaluate the heterogeneous task outputs, we develop a hybrid evaluation protocol combining deterministic programmatic verification for executable artifacts with a calibrated, expert-validated LLM-based judge for textual artifacts. Beyond outcome assessment, we analyze progress and solution stability along execution trajectories to characterize how agents reach their final results. Experiments with 10 frontier LLM agents reveal substantial performance gaps: GPT-6 Astra achieves the highest overall score of 80.9, yet only 26.0% of its runs exceed the 0.95 success threshold. candidates.title: ReMedI: Inference-Time Refinement and Self-Distillation for Controllable Molecular Optimization
candidates.abstract: In drug development, lead optimization must improve competing properties, such as increasing permeability and reducing toxicity, while limiting scaffold changes that could compromise the lead's potency. RL-based post-training, such as C-MORAL, addresses this problem by fine-tuning molecular language models to directly optimize molecular leads for objectives of interest, which relies on expensive task-specific datasets and faces challenges in achieving multi-objective optimization (MOO). We argue a pre-trained model may already contain useful molecular edits that zero-shot generation cannot efficiently reach. Motivated by the limited search capabilities of zero-shot generation, we develop an efficient Metropolis-Hastings search strategy to better explore the proposal distribution. We propose ReMedI, which uses the molecular language model as a base proposer for inference-time alignment. Given a lead and a set of multi-objective tasks, the model proposes edits conditioned on the current molecule, while Metropolis--Hastings refinement guides sequential edits under an objective for property improvement, preservation, and lead similarity. On both C-MuMOInstruct and SMDD benchmarks, refinement improves frozen base models across three backbones, reaching significantly higher multi-objective optimization success rates compared to baselines. These search traces can then distilled into the base model which improves zero-shot generation and subsequent search using approximately 7.8 times less training molecular leads than that of C-MORAL. ReMedI achieves approximately 2.8 times the strict-success coverage of RL baseline C-MORAL, including on out-of-distribution tasks, with matched lead-relative similarity.

candidates.title: Online LLM Inference Routing for Multi-Agent Systems under Long-Term Budget and Layered Privacy Constraints
candidates.abstract: Abstract The Cloud-Edge-End (CEE) collaborative architecture has become a key paradigm for deploying highly intelligent multi-agent systems with low latency and high energy efficiency. Existing studies on efficient task offloading in CEE, however, either overlook long-term financial budget constraints from commercial API token usage and edge computing leasing, or inadequately handle layered information-sharing and privacy restrictions in decentralized autonomous agents. This paper investigates online inference routing to minimize the computational and communication overhead of large language model (LLM) workloads under long-term budget constraints, agent intent-sharing limitations, and un-known future prompt lengths. We propose a budget-aware online optimization framework that uses Lyapunov optimization to decouple long-term financial constraints, and show that the decoupled problem forms a generalized ordinal potential game. To address heterogeneous information-sharing restrictions, we design an adaptive best response algorithm for cooperative environments with shared decision information, and a multi-agent distributed routing algorithm for limited-information environments, enabling efficient offloading without inter-agent intent sharing. Theoretical analysis provides conditional performance and queue-length bounds and establishes finite convergence of the per-slot solvers. Simulations on distributed inference testbeds show that our scheme reduces the inference overhead of heterogeneous agentic tasks while achieving a favorable trade-off between performance and actual token expenditure.

candidates.title: Not All Information Is Worth Asking For: Decision-Informed Information Seeking with LLMs
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support decisions under incomplete information, where deciding what to look up and when to stop matters as much as the final answer. However, LLMs fall into an information trap: They pay for checks, i.e., costly pieces of evidence, that cannot change their decision or are not worth their cost, and they keep asking when the evidence is already sufficient. To this end, we propose Decision-Informed Value-of-information Acquisition (DIVA), a simple yet effective procedure for LLM information seeking based on the decision value of evidence. DIVA 1) lets the LLM specify a small decision model, i.e., how likely a bad outcome is and how each check would shift this probability, through short numeric questions and 2) values each candidate check by how much its imagined outcomes improve the decision net of its cost, stopping when no check is worth its cost. Its variant, DIVA-U, further accounts for the LLM's uncertain estimates of how strongly each check shifts this probability. DIVA is training-free and applies to any LLM. Across four domains and 20 LLMs, DIVA-U has lower regret, i.e., value lost relative to the best possible decision, than every LLM baseline on real-world data, mainly by stopping once evidence suffices, and DIVA cuts the regret of the best LLM baseline by 75% in synthetic scenarios where every check's reliability is given. candidates.title: MusicTwins: Training Audio-Language Models to Listen like Their Persona
candidates.abstract: People differ in how they perceive music, what associations they make with it, what they like about it, and how they respond to it. Computational models intended to simulate people in environments that include music should account for these differences. Although LLMs have been shown to reproduce aspects of human behavior, whether audio-language models (ALMs) can reproduce a specific person's responses to textual and musical stimuli remains underexplored. We introduce MusicTwins, a framework that combines persona summaries, personal memory, and post-training to generate person-specific responses. We construct persona representations from human writings, capturing background, views, personality, writing style, and a musical profile, and post-train Audio Flamingo Next through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Evaluation on ten held-out personas shows notable improvements for Audio Flamingo Next in persona fidelity, including personality, writing style, and responses to music, supporting MusicTwins as a foundation for training audio-language models to listen like their persona.

candidates.title: Monetizing Intelligence: Advertising and Subscription Design on LLM Platforms
candidates.abstract: Large language model (LLM) platforms introducing advertising must decide how much capability ad revenue should fund and what consumers should pay to avoid ads. We study a monopolistic platform that jointly chooses costly response quality, advertising intensity, and subscription prices when advertising reduces user value but better service raises advertising returns. Three findings follow. First, when partly ad-supported and ad-free plans coexist, advertising can finance useful service for consumers who receive none under pure subscription. Lower effective quality in middle plans weakens the alternatives available to premium users, allowing higher prices for unchanged ad-free service. Some fully ad-supported users gain utility, while partly ad-supported and ad-free users lose: broader access can coexist with utility polarization. Second, an intermediate advertising cap can maximize consumer surplus by preserving some revenue that finances service while limiting degradation. Third, cheaper compute can raise quality and reduce ad intensity, yet sufficiently large cost reductions can increase aggregate advertising revenue above its initial level because better service raises the value of the remaining advertised interactions. An extension shows how advertising-funded upgrades can bring plans to the same maximum capability and advertising exposure, eliminating the basis for different prices. These results make menu design central to evaluating LLM advertising: the consequences extend beyond users who see ads to the alternatives and prices faced by those who do not.

candidates.title: MedCaseAgent: From Multimodal Clinical Evidence to Rare Disease Case Reports

MedCaseAgent leverages a hierarchical structure, integrating patient-level data mining with iterative, tool-integrated reasoning. By dynamically querying medical literature and knowledge bases, the agent maintains high clinical fidelity and assesses case novelty. The framework is inherently modular, supporting various backbone LLMs in a plug-and-play fashion. To facilitate this research, we release MedCase-150K, a large-scale multimodal clinical case-report corpus, and MedCase-Bench, a robust temporally held-out evaluation suite. We also introduce an open-source model post-trained from Qwen3.5-9B and optimized specifically for this task. Under both LLM-judged and rule-based evaluation, MedCaseAgent outperforms existing general-purpose and specialized medical LLMs and agents. candidates.title: LGMT: A Tool for Testing the Logical Reasoning Reliability of LLMs
candidates.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly serve as reasoning components in modern software systems, yet a model that answers a logical query correctly can contradict itself when the same problem is restated in an equivalent form. Static benchmarks evaluate queries in isolation and therefore fail to expose such inconsistencies. To address this limitation, we present LGMT, an open-source tool that detects reasoning inconsistencies through metamorphic relations grounded in first-order logic. Given a source test case in premise-conclusion form, LGMT generates logically equivalent follow-up cases and checks whether the model's entailment predictions agree across the pair, without ground-truth labels. The tool provides 20 built-in metamorphic relations, supports custom ones verified by the Z3 theorem prover, and runs from a CLI or a web studio, including an offline mock mode requiring no API key. Across six widely used LLMs on a bundled benchmark of 3,091 metamorphic groups, LGMT reveals inconsistency rates ranging from 20.84% to 29.44%. LGMT is publicly available on GitHub at https://github.com/MaxwelsDonc/lgmt-tool, with a demonstration video at https://youtu.be/gou4opptu1U.

candidates.title: KnitTrans: Coordinated Trajectory Transfer for Effective and Efficient LLM Reinforcement Learning
candidates.abstract: Trajectory transfer from rollout to training affects both learning quality and system efficiency in large language model reinforcement learning (RL). Enforcing batch-wide training requirements can delay the admission of completed trajectories, resulting in higher architectural staleness: the additional parameter-version gap from disaggregated pipelining relative to colocated execution. Beyond admission, misalignment between data access and training consumption causes redundant movement and unnecessary waiting when transferring large trajectory payloads. We present KnitTrans, a system that coordinates the rollout-to-training path through three designs. First, constraint-preserving mini-batch admission allows flexibility in early mini-batch composition, while checking that enough capacity remains to satisfy the remaining quotas. Second, on-demand trajectory data access matches storage units to consumer assignments and overlaps micro-batch data preparation with computation. Third, multimodal encoding deduplication supports reuse across a mini-batch while preserving gradient contributions from all backbone micro-batches. Experiments show up to 93% lower architectural staleness than with train-batch admission, narrowing the learning-quality gap between disaggregated execution and colocated execution. On multimodal workloads, KnitTrans reduces transfer latency by two orders of magnitude and achieves a speedup of up to 5.8 times in transfer plus training over the baseline.

candidates.title: Inference-Time Compute Allocation in LLMs: Dynamic Depth and Token Selection for Efficient Problem Solving
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) deliver impressive performance across diverse natural language processing tasks, but their intensive computation and memory requirements severely restrict real-world deployment, especially on edge devices and in latency-sensitive cloud services. Static inference pipelines execute full layers and full tokens for all inputs, resulting in significant resource waste for simple and routine queries. Although dynamic inference methods have emerged to alleviate this issue, most focus only on either layer-level or token-level optimization, and few provide reliable mechanisms to guarantee bounded performance degradation. In this paper, we propose D²TS-LLM, a unified plug-and-play framework for Dynamic Depth and Token Selection that achieves on-demand computational resource allocation for LLM inference. The framework consists of a multi-dimensional lightweight perceptron for estimating input difficulty and token importance, a joint decision module for adaptive layer activation and token-aware computation reduction, and a lightweight performance monitor with dynamic fallback to ensure performance loss remains within a predefined safe threshold. Extensive experiments on representative LLMs (LLaMA-7B, LLaMA-13B, OPT-6.7B) and five common benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, SQuAD v2.0, CNN/Daily Mail, Alpaca) demonstrate that D²TS-LLM reduces computational cost by 42.3%–61.3% and accelerates inference by 38.2%–55.7% with performance loss controlled below 1%. Compared with representative state-of-the-art dynamic inference, quantization, and cache optimization methods, our approach achieves superior efficiency-performance trade-offs and strong cross-model and cross-dataset generalization.
